name: Legendary Druid
body:
Legendary Druid Circles

Legendary Druid Archetypes
Legendary Druid Circles

Many great powers make human life seem small and irrelevant: the kings who abuse us, the gods who ignore us, the timeless powers who don’t even know we exist. The primal powers of nature are different, because they are always there for us. They have been with us since the beginning and are accessible to all.

There are those among society who have mastered this power and use it for the good of the community. Druids are the natural leaders of many small communities; not by right of conquest or by economic manipulation, by virtue of their power and their willingness to help those around them.

Despite their public lives, druids tend to be secretive about their powers, and don’t always reveal everything they know.

Druids are sometimes called priests of nature, but this is misleading. Priests have personal relationships with their deities: they have faith in their gods. Druids do not.

Worshiping nature is a completely selfish act, as nature does not care or even know a druid is worshiping it. Nature does not offer favors, does not reward faith, and does not differentiate between allies and enemies. A druid seeks to get closer to nature to improve their own life, because to them, nature defines perfection. A druid may worship a nature deity in addition to communing with nature, but like a wizard who worships a god of magic, they are not priests.

As experts in using natural power, druids that are willing to help their fellows find that social status comes to them naturally. The druid who tends their garden and cares not for the world is a rarity, with many societies having druids among their nobility and religious classes. Druids are often effective educators and historians as well, with their natural kinship with other druids making it easy to share knowledge across the world.

Role: Druids can fulfill supportive roles in adventuring parties. Their magic is naturally suited towards spells that support, change, empower and heal. That isn’t to say that druids cannot take more direct, offensive, or violent routes; their connections to animals and ability to change shapes allow them to directly enter the fray. Regardless of how they manifest their powers, druids are largely welcome in adventuring parties.

Legendary Class: The legendary cleric’s component elements are similar in nature to the base version of the class but have been heavily adjusted to offer advancements at every level beyond spellcasting, give domains more prominence as a feature, and offer more choices throughout character progression.

Alignment: Any neutral

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The legendary druid’s class skills are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks Per Level: 4 + Int Modifier

Class features

The following are the class features of the legendary druid.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Legendary druids are proficient with the following weapons: club, dagger, dart, quarterstaff, scimitar, scythe, sickle, shortbow, shortspear, sling, and spear. They are also proficient with all natural attacks (claw, bite, and so forth) of any form they assume.

Legendary druids are proficient with light and medium armor and with shields (except tower shields).

Spellcasting

A legendary druid casts divine spells drawn primarily from the legendary druid spell list. They can cast any spell they know without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, a legendary druid must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a legendary druid’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the legendary druid’s Wisdom modifier.

A legendary druid can only cast a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table 1-1: Legendary Druid Class Features. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Wisdom score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells).

A legendary druid must spend 1 hour each day in a trance-like meditation on the mysteries of nature to regain their daily allotment of spells.

A legendary druid’s selection of spells is extremely limited. A legendary druid begins play knowing four 0-level spells (not including a fifth 0-level spell granted by their animal messenger class feature) and three 1st-level spells of their choice. At each new legendary druid level, they gain one or more new spells, as indicated on Table 1-2: Legendary Druid Spells Known. (Unlike spells per day, the number of spells a legendary druid knows is not affected by their Wisdom score; the numbers on Table: Legendary druid Spells Known are fixed.) All of these spells are selected from the legendary druid’s spell list.

Upon reaching a new legendary druid level, a legendary druid can choose to learn a new spell in place of one they already know. In effect, the legendary druid loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. A legendary druid may swap any number of spells at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that they gain new spells known for the level.

A legendary druid does not increase the casting time of their spells by applying metamagic to them.

Orisons: Druids learns a number of orisons, or 0-level spells, each day as noted on Table 1-2: Legendary Druid Spells Known. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again.

Legendary Druid Spell List: The legendary druid spell list includes all spells from the druid spell list, plus the following spells:

2nd Level: alter self
3rd Level: beast shape I
4th Level: adjustable polymorph, beast shape II, elemental body I
5th Level: beast shape III, elemental body II, plant shape I
6th Level: beast shape IV, elemental body III, plant shape II
7th Level: elemental body IV, giant form I, magical beast shape, plant shape III
8th Level: giant form II
Animal Messenger (Ex)

To aid in communication with other legendary druids, all legendary druids gain animal messenger as a 0-level orison known. This is in addition to the 4 0-level spells known at 1st level. This orison cannot be retrained for a different orison.

Bonus Languages

A legendary druid’s bonus language options include Sylvan, the language of woodland creatures.

This choice is in addition to the bonus languages available to the character because of their race.

A legendary druid also knows Druidic, which they learn upon becoming a 1st-level legendary druid in addition to their regular allotment of languages. Druidic works as a language but is actually an intuitive form of communication that can incorporate words, movements, simple markings, and even smells. Although it has its written alphabet, it can be used with other languages, and even without conventional language at all.

Legendary druids are forbidden to teach this language to non-legendary druids, and most non legendary druids lack the necessary knowledge anyway.

Druidic Circle (Ex)

A legendary druid’s circles are the primary powers provided to them by nature. Each circle also provides them with additional spells known. These spells cannot be retrained to different spells known. The legendary druid may select one circle. Once chosen, it cannot be changed.

Druidic Order (Ex)

Unlike other classes, legendary druids have a specific relationship with others of their kind that extends to all legendary druids. Although legendary druids can be on opposite sides in a conflict (usually resulting from their relationships with others), there is an understanding between them that they all serve a greater purpose, and they can never be true enemies. Even if one seriously harms the other, there is unlikely to be lasting enmity.

The legendary druidic order is the informal community of legendary druids that spans the world. All legendary druids, by virtue of the secrets they share and the language they speak, have some kinship with the order, even if they do not interact with it regularly. The order has no official structure, but the greatest legendary druids – the hierophants – are able to wield considerable influence through it.

While on their home plane of existence, the legendary druid can request help from the order for various purposes. To do so, they can speak to other legendary druids directly, leave hidden messages in locations where they know legendary druids will see it, or cast spells such as animal messenger. If none of these are options, they may make a plea while recovering their spell slots. They may make as many requests as they like. The response time will be determined by the type of request.

Request Shelter: If the legendary druid is able to find a legendary druid encampment, shrine, or holy place maintained by other legendary druids, they can require food and shelter for themselves and their allies. The value of such shelter is roughly 1 to 5 gp per day, depending on how wealthy the legendary druids are.
Request Information: The legendary druid can request information from the order. This can be any information a person could make with a knowledge check. The order then makes a knowledge check to see if it has access to this information. For this purpose, the order is trained in all knowledge skills and has a knowledge of 30. The legendary druid can expect a response within 1d6 days.
Request Materials: The legendary druid can use their legendary druidic connections to request rare and exotic materials. This can include basic supplies, rare herbs, samples of various natural materials, and even drugs or poisons. The legendary druid must still pay for these items. The chance of an item being available is 100% – 1% for every 10gp the item is worth.

This request requires someone to physically visit the legendary druid and therefore can take up to 3d6 days to see a response, successful or not. If it is not successful, it cannot be requested again for 3 months.

At 3rd level, the legendary druid can attempt to request scrolls of legendary druid spells, or potions that duplicate them. The chance of a scroll being available is 100% – 5% for every caster level of the scroll or potion. The legendary druid may request the highest level available, in which case the GM rolls a d20, and if that number is a caster level high enough to produce the item, then the legendary druid receives it with a caster level equal to that roll.

At 7th level, the legendary druid can request rare materials, including unusual metals, rare poisons, or any non-magical item they could find for sale anywhere. This works the same as requesting common materials, with the chance of an item being available being 100% – 1% for every 100gp it is worth.

At 11th level, the legendary druid gains a 10% discount on all requested materials. In addition, requests now only take 2d6 days.

At 15th level, the legendary druid can request anything non-magical for sale anywhere. This can include samples of dragon blood, non-unique magic items, and the occasional soul. The chance of an item being available is 100% – 1% for every 1,000 gp it is worth.

At 19th level, the legendary druid can make requests while on any of the inner planes, not just their home plane of existence. Requests now only take 1d6 days.

Eschew Materials

A legendary druid gains Eschew Materials as a bonus feat at 1st level.

Wildspeak (Ex)

A legendary druid is skilled in speaking with creatures that are close to nature. They can speak with any creature with the animal or magical beast type or communicate with them as if they spoke their language if they don’t have one. In addition, they gain a bonus equal to half their class level (minimum 1) to Diplomacy checks against such creatures when attempting to influence their attitude.

As a legendary druid grows more experienced, they learn to communicate with more exotic creatures. At 5th level, they may use this ability with any creature of the monstrous humanoid or fey types, at 9th level, they may use this ability with vermin and plants, at 13th level, they may use this ability with elementals and oozes.

At 17th level, they may speak with the earth itself, communicating with rocks, rivers, and soil as if they were intelligent. For this purpose, treat each 30 ft by 30 ft section of earth as a separate intelligent creature, unless an obvious physical landmark is larger than that, with an alignment and temperament befitting that sort of terrain. The earth is aware of what has happened to it, and has some understanding of events that have occurred in its presence (though it doesn’t speak common languages).

Druidic Talents

At 2nd level, the legendary druid gains a minor druidic talent. They gain additional minor talents at 4th, 6th, and 8th level.

At 10th level, they gain their first major talent, and may choose additional major talents at 12th, 14th, and 16th level. A minor talent may be chosen in place of a major talent.

At 18th level, the legendary druid gains a grand talent, and they gain another one at 20th level. They may choose a major or minor talent in place of either or both grant talents.

Soul Seed (Ex)

At 19th level, the legendary druid undergoes a ceremony where they transfer part of their soul to the earth itself. Whenever the legendary druid dies from something other than old age, after 24 hours their body disintegrates, and they emerge from the earth in a different location on their home plane of existence, as if affected by true resurrection.

Hierophant (Ex)

At 20th level, the legendary druid’s power is recognized among all legendary druids, and they join the ranks of the leaders of the legendary druidic order: the hierophants. Their new rank puts them on the same level as kings, and the hierophant can safely expect those who know who they are to treat them with a high degree of respect.

As a leader of the legendary druidic order, the hierophant can command the order to perform certain tasks that are beyond the scope of even the greatest individual casters.

Legendary druids lead by doing, however, so the hierophant must be willing to perform the task themselves. Once per month, the hierophant can perform a task and then command the order to dispatch legendary druids to repeat the same task en masse. If the legendary druid can perform their task successfully, then the dispatched legendary druids will (mostly) succeed as well. A hierophant can destroy nations (and create them), relocate mountains one stone at a time, and change the political structure of the world.

For logistical reasons, these tasks must be limited to the hierophant’s home plane of existence.

In addition, the hierophant is given resources for personal use. Once per month, including upon receiving this rank, the legendary druid can ask for a miracle to be cast on their behalf, for any purpose they desire. They do not need to provide the material component for the spell.
